curriculum.title: Incarnation and the Identity of Jesus

core.big_idea: The incarnation joins genuine humanity, divine identity, humility, obedience, and exaltation.

passages.reading_note: Read in context; use age-appropriate portions without changing the claim.
Read in context; use age-appropriate portions without changing the claim.

core.metanarrative_position: Jesus’ identity is explored through incarnation, humanity, divine identity, humility, obedience, and exaltation
core.biblical_genre: Johannine prologue and Pauline Christological passage

claims.statement: John says the Word became flesh and lived among us.
Philippians describes Christ Jesus in humility, servanthood, obedience unto death, and exaltation.
The term incarnation may summarize the biblical claim that the divine Word truly became human, while Scripture remains the doctrinal foundation.
claims.interpretive_hinge: This conclusion depends on the approved curriculum framework and its distinction between direct text, synthesis, inference, and age-appropriate application; Scripture does not directly mandate this exact curriculum formulation.
claims.prohibited_overstatement: Do not present this framework conclusion as an explicit biblical command or quotation.

core.interpretation_skill: Observe text; reconstruct context; account for genre; distinguish text, synthesis, inference, and application

learning.foundation_objective: Analyse the relevant text and explain the case that the incarnation joins genuine humanity, divine identity, humility, obedience, and exaltation.
learning.extension_objective: Test the claim against context, genre, canonical synthesis, credible alternatives, and the limits of the available evidence.
know: The incarnation joins genuine humanity, divine identity, humility, obedience, and exaltation.
understand: Meaning depends on immediate context, genre, and available evidence.
Direct observation should remain distinct from synthesis, inference, framework position, prudential judgment, and application.
practise: State at least one observation before interpretation.
Separate statements into text, synthesis, and later theological term and explain the distinction.
become: A learner who reads Scripture carefully and responds with trust, wisdom, worship, service, and love.
success_evidence: Student can support the big idea with evidence.
Student can distinguish observation from interpretation or application.

preparation.passage_context: Jesus’ identity is explored through incarnation, humanity, divine identity, humility, obedience, and exaltation

John says the Word became flesh and lived among us.

interpretation_notes: Start with the selected passage before moving to synthesis or application.
Keep genre, audience, historical setting, and literary context visible.
Distinguish direct text, synthesis, inference, framework positions, prudential judgments, and application.
theological_guardrails: Do not imply Jesus only appeared human.
Do not claim the word “incarnation” occurs in the passage.
Do not reduce Philippians 2 to metaphysics and miss its ethical appeal to humility.

accessibility.reading_level: Teen independent or guided close reading
accessibility.plain_language_rule: Define unfamiliar terms before theological shorthand.
neurodiversity_supports: Allow students to pass on personal-sharing questions.
non_reader_support: Read aloud and use icons, sequence cards, oral choices, or a scribe.

do_not_ask: Do not require disclosure of trauma, family finances, grief, or private spiritual decisions.
Do not pressure a child or young person toward baptism, public prayer, or another public response.
safeguarding.teacher_response: Answer from the evidence, acknowledge uncertainty where needed, and route personal or safety concerns to appropriate adults.
